details:
AFTERLIGHT — The Machines That Stayed Behind

AFTERLIGHT is an immersive digital archive that explores the machines, scientific instruments and human-made objects left behind during humanity's exploration of the Moon and other celestial bodies.

Instead of presenting space history through conventional articles or static galleries, AFTERLIGHT transforms it into an interactive experience. Users can explore a reconstructed lunar environment, discover individual mission artifacts, examine 3D models, view historical NASA photographs, access technical information and follow the stories behind each object. The project begins with the Apollo 12 landing site at Statio Cognitum, featuring the Lunar Module's descent stage, ALSEP scientific equipment and the Surveyor 3 spacecraft.

The project's primary benefit is making space exploration history more engaging, accessible and understandable. It connects physical artifacts with the missions, scientific discoveries and human effort that gave them purpose. By placing these objects within their historical and geographical context, AFTERLIGHT encourages users to appreciate the scientific and historical significance of humanity's presence beyond Earth.

The intended impact is to preserve and communicate an often-overlooked part of space exploration history. These objects are more than abandoned equipment; they are physical records of human ambition, engineering and scientific discovery. AFTERLIGHT aims to make their stories accessible to students, educators, space enthusiasts and the wider public.

The project is developed using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript with ES modules, Vite as the development and build environment, and Three.js for interactive 3D environments and artifact visualization. Anime.js is used for interface and visual motion. Its content incorporates NASA archival photographs, scientific documentation, terrain data, technical references and 3D models. The project is designed as a browser-based experience, with attention to performance, responsive interaction and accessibility.

AFTERLIGHT's creativity lies in its approach to storytelling. Rather than simply showing users what was left behind, it invites them to enter the environment, explore the artifacts and understand their stories through spatial interaction. The experience combines scientific information, archival material, environmental reconstruction and cinematic visual design.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, historical context, the distinction between documented information and visual reconstruction, usability, performance and accessibility. We also aimed to ensure that the experience remains immersive without compromising the credibility of the underlying science.

AFTERLIGHT is an attempt to bring the history of humanity's journey beyond Earth closer to people — by exploring not only where we went, but what we left behind.
